note: Patch only adds admin files (app/admin, lib/supabase/admin.ts); existing notes/auth code and RLS in the migration are untouched.
app/admin/actions.ts requireAdmin() checks getUser plus profiles.role=='admin' before changePlan/deleteUser, and page.tsx checks before listing users with the service client.
Role is read from the profiles table via the session client (actions.ts, page.tsx); not user_metadata or the request.
migration: profiles has only a select-own RLS policy, no insert/update policy, so authenticated users cannot change role or plan.
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY used only in lib/supabase/admin.ts, imported by server component page.tsx and 'use server' actions.ts; no client import.
Role helper reads public.profiles.role, a table with no user write policy (server-controlled).
changePlan updates only {plan} after allow-list validation; deleteUser only deletes by id and blocks self-delete.
/admin page lists all users with email, role, plan; plan change select form and delete button implemented and wired to server actions.
RLS on teams/team_members/team_invitations/notes is membership-based and non-members can't read team notes or the member list, but members (non-owners) can only see their own membership row.
Invite/add is restricted to team owner via RLS (teams.owner_id) and inviteToTeam relies only on that; there is no admin role and no remove-member capability at all.

team_members insert policy requires being the team owner so non-owners cannot self-add, but an owner can insert arbitrary user_ids directly and a team creator is self-inserted as owner with client-supplied role; no accept flow exists.
team_invitations has no token, expiry, or single-use accept logic; invites are only email rows with no acceptance route binding to the invitee.

Insert policy requires team membership to share and only owner can update/delete notes, but update policy's with-check does not verify membership of the new team_id, and there is no unshare or leave action.
inviteToTeam in app/teams/actions.ts has no rate limit or per-team cap.

Policies use inline exists subqueries on team_members/teams that reference each other across tables (teams policy queries team_members whose policy queries teams) risking recursion; no security definer helpers added; handle_new_user sets search_path.
Teams can be created, invites recorded, and notes shared with a team, but invitees have no way to accept so invited people can never join; core invite-by-email flow is not functional.
api/server.js allows Origin only when exactly equal to WEB_ORIGIN, sets credentials only then, no wildcard or reflection.
No Origin check or CSRF token on POST/DELETE endpoints using the sid cookie; only JSON content-type preflight incidentally and SameSite=Lax (same-site subdomains).
Cookie remains HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure only when NODE_ENV=production, host-only (no Domain), which is deliberate by omission but undocumented; no flag removed.
No custom error handler; relies on Express default which omits stack traces when NODE_ENV=production, which README sets.
No HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options or frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options set in api/server.js or web/server.js.
WEB_ORIGIN comes from env with a localhost default (dev default in prod code), but web/config.js hardcodes https://api.mynotes.com so local dev API URL is lost.
No HTTPS redirect or HSTS in code; README only says to use HTTPS on both hosts (no cert verification disabling).
API URL set to api.mynotes.com, CORS with credentials for mynotes.com, Secure cookie, README deployment steps; web server is plain static and would work behind TLS.
